blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile portrait card/deployment tower defense with story and survival modes
- objective: defend the player base while deploying units/spells from a rotating hand to destroy the rival base or survive waves
- input model: one-thumb pointer/touch; tap cards to select, tap lower half to deploy units, tap anywhere for spells, tap scrap for partial energy refund
- core loop: energy regenerates, player spends energy on cards, AI spends energy on enemy units, units path toward bridges/targets, attacks reduce HP, enemy kills grant persistent currency, story stages escalate enemy HP/AI speed/boss pressure
- fail/friction state: player tower destroyed or story timer expires; insufficient energy and invalid enemy-half deployment produce feedback toasts

## Protected mechanics
- Preserve card selection, four-card hand, next-card cycling, energy cost/refund, lower-half deployment rule for units, spell permissiveness, AI spawning, tower HP bars, projectile/melee contact, gold rewards, story progression, survival waves, upgrades, win/loss semantics, and mobile pointer controls.
- Preserve story timer with final 60-second energy surge and survival increasing wave timer.
- Preserve canvas loop and hit/proximity style rather than replacing with unrelated mechanics.

## Remixed target
Tower Defense. A satirical game inspired by anime lo-fi neon city built around tower defense play, with competitive, creative, skill based energy, with friends session design, search-friendly hooks like tower defense, strategy, defense, aesthetics like neon aesthetic, anime aesthetic, chrome aesthetic, and meme-tone cues such as gyatt, tryhard. Designed for one-thumb mobile play with touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, fast onboarding, and portrait-first UX tuned for iOS and Android in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

The canonical rebuilt surface is **Gyatt Grid Defense**, a neon anime lo-fi city tower-defense game where the player protects a glowing rooftop lo-fi core from rival-feed tryhard bots. Mechanics remain the source tower-defense loop, while the world, HUD vocabulary, procedural city, unit silhouettes, chrome cards, meme-tone feedback, fonts, and mobile onboarding are fully reauthored.
